programs.summary: The research pipeline's preparation of FinGPT: cleaning, the nine shades to three classes, duplicates folded, a group key.
programs.what: Reads data/raw/fs_train.csv, repairs the Windows-1252 mojibake, applies NFC, strips zero-width characters and normalises whitespace while keeping punctuation. Maps the nine sentiment shades to negative, neutral and positive and keeps the shade in its own column. Folds exact duplicates into one row with a count and gives every row a near-duplicate group so that no split ever separates two versions of the same sentence. Writes one table per set with a content hash.
depends: scripts in the research pipeline share one config file

arch.d: shade kept in its own column

meetings.note: Prepared tables walked through on the call: 374 mojibake repairs and 2 label conflicts shown.

programs.summary: The first encoding pass: bge-large-en-v1.5 frozen, fp16 on one P100, 2,048 values per text, cached under a content hash.
programs.what: Loads the encoder offline from the Hugging Face cache, reads every prepared text in windows of 510 tokens with a 32-token overlap, pools the [CLS] vector joined with the masked mean over the tokens, averages the windows of a long text and stores the result as float16 under the SHA-256 of the weights, the tokenizer, the text column, the pooling and the length settings. A second run with the same inputs finds the cache and does nothing. 30,209 texts took 1.8 minutes.

arch.d: one P100, token budget per batch

meetings.note: Encoding time far under the A2 estimate: 1.8 minutes for the whole corpus.

programs.summary: The first model on the SuperComputer: a multinomial logit on the frozen features. 57 percent on our own training set.
programs.what: Fits a multinomial logistic regression on the cached 2,048 features and scores it on the training set and on SEntFiN. The 57 percent on our own training rows, and worse on the test, is the result that started the four-day investigation and the paper study. The script stayed in the research pipeline as the ancestor of the linear control.

meetings.note: 57 percent on our own training set, worse on the test; the investigation agreed on the spot.

programs.summary: The data investigation of 7 to 10 October: how the encoder's position moves when a sentence changes polarity.
programs.what: Takes pairs of sentences that differ in polarity and measures how far the pooled vector moves, on the training set and on the SEntFiN headlines, and compares the training labels with the encoder's nearest neighbours. It showed that the information is there but a single linear boundary does not read it, and that the training labels themselves were part of the problem. Its write-up opened Sprint 1.

arch.d: grew against fell, and the like
the labels are part of the problem

meetings.note: The information is there; a single linear boundary does not read it.
Sprint 1 planned on the strength of the read-out: a deep learning pipeline.

programs.summary: Johnny's cleaning and exploratory analysis of the general dataset (emotion-emotion_69k.csv): skew, anomalies, quality charts.
programs.what: Loads the general emotion dataset, cleans it, renames the files to say what they hold, and draws the class skew and the anomaly charts the team used for its quality check. The exploration fed the data-quality follow-up of the label audit; the general-domain models built on it were exploratory only.

meetings.note: Quality charts reviewed on the first call of the week.

programs.summary: A logistic regression on TF-IDF features for the general domain. Explored, then walked back.
programs.what: Johnny's experimental general-domain model: TF-IDF features and a logistic regression on the general dataset. It was built to explore, not to deliver, and was dropped once the frozen-encoder route was chosen. Its role as a bag-of-words control passed to the word logit of the final repository, on the finance corpora.

meetings.note: Explored only; not for the delivery.

programs.note: Walked back on 10 October: the word logit of the final repository is the bag-of-words control.

programs.summary: Pairwise similarity of the 32 encoded emotion labels, drawn as a heatmap. Dropped: the intensity pairs sit on top of each other.
programs.what: Encodes the 32 emotion label names with the encoder, computes their pairwise cosine similarity and draws it with seaborn, with a batch size limit added to the encoding. The heatmap showed that afraid and terrified, angry and furious, sad and devastated are indistinguishable to the encoder, which is one reason the valence route was dropped.

meetings.note: The intensity pairs sit on top of each other; the route was dropped.

programs.summary: A softmax over the encoded emotion labels to derive a sentiment: the A2 valence idea. Replaced by distillation.
programs.what: The Assignment 2 plan read sentiment off an emotion head through Warriner's valence groups. This script tried the first step on the general dataset: a softmax over the similarities of a text to the encoded emotion labels, mapped to a sentiment. It was replaced by distillation: the FinGPT Network reads every dialogue window once and its readings become the sentiment column the Dialogue Network learns.

meetings.note: Walked back; the dialogue head gets a learned sentiment output instead.

programs.note: Replaced on 18 October by the distilled sentiment column of the dialogue windows.

programs.summary: The check that dismissed the Kaggle Finance News Sentiments file as a test set: undocumented labels, 93 against 46 percent agreement.
programs.what: Johnny flagged the Benedetti file: undocumented labels and an overlap with FinGPT. Ricky's label analysis confirmed it: the same head agrees with 93 percent of its rows that are also in FinGPT and 46 percent of the rest, so the labels are not learnable in the way SEntFiN's are. SEntFiN 1.0 stayed the external test.
affects: the dataset table of the design document
writes: section II.F of the design document

meetings.note: Dismissed as a test set; SEntFiN 1.0 stays the external test.

programs.summary: The Assignment 2 plan: full fine-tuning of the 335M encoder for M1 to M3 and a DoRA adapter for M4. Never written.
programs.what: Assignment 2 proposed letting the sentiment gradient reach the attention and feed-forward matrices, with micro-batches of 16, gradient checkpointing and fp16 loss scaling on the P100, about 35 GPU-hours. The cost check of 29 and 30 September and the frozen-feature literature (Kumar et al. 2022) decided against it, Dr Vo agreed the scope cut by email, and the encoder stayed frozen.
depends: the P100: 12 GB, fp16 only, no tensor cores

meetings.note: Scope cut confirmed with Dr Vo by email; access under his project.

programs.note: Cancelled before the sprints: the encoder is frozen throughout.

programs.summary: UMAP, GMM and CKA on the fine-tuned spaces, as planned in A2. With the encoder frozen the space is fixed, so the head is inspected instead.
programs.what: The Assignment 2 representation analysis compared the pooled space before and after fine-tuning. With a frozen encoder there is no second space to compare, so the analysis moved to the head: the random-label control, the label audit, the Hessian, seed connectivity and probes of fd_10.

meetings.note: With the encoder frozen the space is fixed; the head is what we inspect.

programs.note: Replaced by the head inspection of fd_10_nn_inspect.py.

programs.summary: The head search on FinGPT under the protocol: 34 configurations, successive halving, 15 runs each. The first network memorised; c12 came out.
programs.what: Stage one of the research pipeline for the network heads. The first feed-forward head on the cached features memorised its training set: training accuracy kept climbing while held-out accuracy fell. The paper study that followed set the protocol: a confirmation split held out by group before anything is fitted, StratifiedGroupKFold five by three seeds, label smoothing, an exponential moving average of the weights, early stopping on the validation cross-entropy, a temperature fitted on the out-of-fold logits. The search ran as the job of Monday 19 October (59 minutes) and chose c12: 2,048 to 256 leaky ReLU to 128 tanh to 3, 557,827 weights, 0.8044 macro-F1 cross-validated, 0.798 on the confirmation split.

arch.d: AdamW, warm-up, cosine, EMA, early stop

meetings.note: The first network memorises its training set.
Sprint 1 review: the protocol taken from the papers, page by page.
c12 at 0.8044 cross-validated and 0.798 on the confirmation split.

programs.summary: The label audit and the random-label control: every validation row's predicted class recorded, the head on shuffled labels.
programs.what: Records the predicted class of every validation row across the 15 runs so the rows the head never learns can be read, and trains the same head on shuffled labels to show how much of the training accuracy is memorisation. Johnny's data-quality follow-up on the audited rows named the convention gap between the annotators.
affects: the data section of the design document

meetings.note: Audit reviewed; the convention gap named.

programs.summary: The inspection of the chosen head: Hessian trace, seed connectivity, linear probes. Eleven minutes.
programs.what: What replaced the representation analysis of Assignment 2. With the encoder frozen the space does not change, so the head is examined: the trace of the Hessian at the solution, whether the solutions of different seeds connect along a low-loss path, and what linear probes read from each hidden layer.
affects: the analysis section of the design document

meetings.note: Sprint 2 review: the full model research demonstrated.

programs.summary: Zero-shot transfer to SEntFiN and the prior corrections: EM, BBSE and balanced all lost to the uncorrected probabilities.
programs.what: Scores the FinGPT Network on the 10,532 labelled SEntFiN headlines without any adaptation (73.5 percent) and applies the three prior corrections proposed in Assignment 2. They reach 0.643, 0.669 and 0.734 against 0.735 uncorrected: the SEntFiN errors are a convention shift, not a change of class mix, so no prior correction repairs them and none ships.

meetings.note: Uncorrected probabilities kept; the errors are a convention shift.

programs.summary: The dialogue windows: two turns in conversation order, the FinGPT Network's reading as the sentiment column, 64,566 windows encoded.
programs.what: Builds two-turn windows of EmpatheticDialogues in conversation order, keeps the speaker's emotion (32 classes) and adds the sentiment column by distillation: the FinGPT Network reads every window once (negative 3.9 percent, neutral 85.6, positive 10.5). Groups are conversations, so no split separates two windows of one conversation. The windows are encoded on the P100 in 3.9 minutes.

meetings.note: Sprint 3 planning: the Dialogue Network and the reinforcement suite.

programs.summary: The Dialogue Network search: one trunk, two outputs (sentiment and 32 emotions). Job of Sunday 25 October, 141 minutes; c31 chosen.
programs.what: The same protocol as fd_07 with two readings from one trunk: the loss is the sum of the two readings' cross-entropies with the emotion term weighted, the folds are grouped by conversation, and one temperature is fitted per reading. c31 came out: 2,048 to 256 ReLU to 128 SiLU to 32 ELU to [3 | 32], 562,723 weights, 0.8555 sentiment and 0.3723 emotion macro-F1 cross-validated, 74.5 percent on SEntFiN without ever seeing a finance label.

meetings.note: The Dialogue Network reviewed on the Sunday call.
Live-testing check: the two readings from one trunk.

programs.summary: The reinforcement suite: the closed form, leashed SFT, REINFORCE, GRPO, PPO and a Q layer, full-information and bandit feedback, 36 runs.
programs.what: Formulates adaptation as a contextual bandit under a KL leash with a retention term, then runs every method on every corpus, before and after: the closed form of the leashed objective, leashed supervised fine-tuning, REINFORCE, GRPO, PPO with the ratio clipped to [0.8, 1.2], a Q layer, and the bandit variants with the off-policy estimators on the log. The job of 25 October 15:47 ran 22 adaptation runs in 9 minutes 19 seconds. REINFORCE, PPO and the Q layer tied with GRPO or fell behind it when every label is known, so only the closed form and GRPO went into the final repository.

meetings.note: Gains and retention reviewed method by method.
Sprint 3 review: only the closed form and GRPO ship.

programs.summary: The misread rows only: the selection-bias experiment. The closed form gains 6.8 points for 0.3 lost; every sampled method learned never neutral.
programs.what: Trains only on the rows of the training half that the starting head misreads. The closed form reaches 80.3 percent on the held-out half for 0.3 FinGPT points lost. The sampled methods on the same rows all learned to avoid neutral and ended below where they started: a biased sample, so the setting ships for the closed form only, as --rows wrong of adapt.py.

arch.n: misread rows of the training half

meetings.note: A biased sample for the sampled methods; kept for the closed form only.

programs.summary: One configuration per corpus: the files, the labels, the head, the protocol and the adaptation settings.
programs.what: Everything a script needs to know about a corpus: the raw files and the prediction sets, the readings with their label maps, the head (widths, activations, dropout, weight decay), the protocol (confirmation fraction 0.15, 5 folds, 3 seeds, 100 epochs, patience 10, warm-up 1, cosine floor 0.1, EMA 0.999) and the adaptation block (beta 0.3, beta_grpo 0.1, group 4, retain 1, 20 epochs, lr 3e-4, batch 256, holdout 0.5). The dialogue config adds the emotion reading and grouping by conversation.

meetings.note: Lean repository agreed: one config file per corpus.

programs.summary: The environment: the project root and offline flags every shell and job source, and the venv built once on the cluster's Python module.
programs.what: paths.sh exports the project root, the Hugging Face cache, the offline flags and the venv; setup.sh builds the venv on the loaded Python module, installs torch from the CUDA 12.6 wheels (the last that run on the P100), the packages and the encoder, and records the module name in venv/PYMOD so every job loads the same one. The first chain submission of 2 November had built the venv on the node's own Python 3.9 with CUDA 12.8 wheels, which dropped the P100; the rebuild on python/3.11.5 fixed it.

meetings.note: First chain submission on Python 3.9 with the CUDA 12.8 wheels: jobs cancelled, environment rebuilt.

programs.summary: The folder layout under the project root: root(), load_config(), cache_dir(), results_dir().
programs.what: Every path a script touches goes through this module, so no absolute path appears in any tracked file. load_config finds a config as a path, as a name under configs/, or as a name under the project root, which is where the smoke chain writes its tiny configs.

meetings.note: Walkthrough of the lean repository at the live-testing check.

programs.summary: Cleaning, label normalisation, duplicate keys, groups and the grouped splits.
programs.what: fix_mojibake and clean_text repair and normalise a text; normalise_labels maps a column onto a reading's classes; near_duplicate_keys and run_keys build the group keys; grouped_folds and confirmation_split hold groups together across every split. UT-D and UT-N test every branch against closed-form answers.

meetings.note: Walkthrough of the lean repository.

programs.summary: The content-hash feature cache: the key, the manifest, save and load.
programs.what: sha256_file and sha256_column digest the weights, the tokenizer and the text column; feature_key joins them with the pooling and the length settings; save_features writes pooled.npy in float16 with ids.csv and a manifest; load_features returns the cache or None. No hostname, working directory or job id goes into the manifest.

meetings.note: Walkthrough of the lean repository.

programs.summary: Offline loading of the encoder, pooling, and the windowed forward pass.
programs.what: model_dir and weights_file find the encoder in the offline cache; digests hash the weights and the tokenizer for the cache key; load puts the model on the device in eval mode; pool joins the [CLS] vector with the masked mean; encode reads long texts in windows of 510 tokens with a 32-token overlap under a token budget and averages the windows. UT-E tests the window count at 1, 509, 510, 511, 988 and 989 tokens.

meetings.note: Walkthrough of the lean repository.

programs.summary: The head, standardisation, the training loop, inference and the JSON form the application reads.
programs.what: MultiHead is a trunk of linear layers with one output layer per reading. standardise fits mean and sd on the training rows; fit runs AdamW with a one-epoch warm-up and a cosine floor, an EMA of the weights, smoothed cross-entropy and early stopping on the validation cross-entropy; predict_logits and predict_proba run inference with the temperatures; to_json and from_json are the export, float16 weights with the activations and temperatures, that the numpy pass, the integration checker and the application all read.

arch.d: mean and sd on the training rows
AdamW, warm-up, cosine floor, EMA, early stop

meetings.note: Export format agreed with Hara: mean, sd, trunk, outputs, temperatures.

programs.summary: Accuracy, macro-F1, log-loss, AUC, confusion, the bootstrap, the corrected resampled t-test and the temperature.
programs.what: evaluate returns every metric of a prediction table; bootstrap_macro_f1 gives the interval of the confirmation score; corrected_resampled_t is Nadeau and Bengio's test on paired fold-by-seed differences with the variance corrected for the overlap of training sets; fit_temperature finds the scalar that divides the logits; ece the calibration error over 15 bins.

meetings.note: The corrected t-test on known values at the live-testing check.

programs.summary: A prepared table with its cached features and its labels, in one call.
programs.what: load_set reads the prepared table of a set, finds its features under the content hash and returns the frame, the feature matrix and the label arrays per reading; labels maps the columns onto the readings' classes.

arch.d: from the config and the texts

meetings.note: Walkthrough of the lean repository.

programs.summary: The dated PASS/FAIL log every test layer and the chain write: one line per check, a .json mirror, no host or path.
programs.what: RunLog opens <stage>_<date>.log and its .json mirror under logs/, writes a header with the reference of the design document, one dated line per check with its id, message and seconds, counts the verdicts and closes with the PASS or FAIL summary line and the exit code. The forbidden-pattern scan keeps hosts, logins and paths out of it.

meetings.note: Log format shown at the live-testing check; the same line in every layer.

programs.summary: Step 1: clean, normalise the labels, fold duplicates, group, and write one table per set with a content hash. Seconds, on the login node.
programs.what: For one config: reads the raw training file and every prediction file, cleans the text, puts the labels on their configured names, folds exact duplicates of the training set with a count, assigns groups (near-duplicate key for finance, conversation for dialogue) and writes the prepared tables with a manifest, label counts and a length audit (how_short). CH-01 of the chain: 6 seconds for both corpora.

meetings.note: Walkthrough of the lean repository.

programs.summary: Step 2: the frozen encoder over every prepared set, fp16 on one GPU; skips a set whose key is in the cache. CH-02: 33 seconds.
programs.what: For each prepared set of a config it computes the feature key from the encoder digests, the text column, the pooling and the length settings, loads the cache if the key exists and otherwise runs the windowed forward pass and saves the features. On 3 November the three caches were found under their hashes, so the job took 33 seconds (7.8 GPU-minutes when they were first written).

meetings.note: Walkthrough of the lean repository.

programs.summary: Steps 3 to 7: confirmation split, StratifiedGroupKFold 5 x 3 on the chosen configuration, temperature, final fit, confirmation scored once, export.
programs.what: Holds the confirmation split out first, runs the grouped folds by seed on the fixed configuration and records every validation fold in folds.csv (read by the controls and the integration test), fits one temperature per reading on the out-of-fold logits, refits on all development rows for the median best epoch, scores the confirmation split once with a bootstrap interval and exports the head. CH-03 and CH-04 of the chain: 9 min 10 s for finance, 6 min 25 s for dialogue; both networks came back to the fourth decimal of the research pipeline's numbers.

arch.d: 15 percent by group, held out first
median best epoch, all development rows

meetings.note: train.py walked through against Appendix B.
The two networks reproduce to the fourth decimal.

programs.summary: A trained head on every prediction set: pieces averaged per original row, metrics where labels exist. Seconds, inside the train job.
programs.what: Loads the exported head, runs it on the cached features of each prediction set, averages the pieces of a long text per original row, writes predictions.csv with the probabilities of every reading and metrics.json with a confusion matrix where the set has labels. sbatch slurm/predict.sh <config> prepares and encodes a new file under data/raw/predict/ first.

meetings.note: predict.py walked through.

programs.summary: Step 8: the leashed objective in two forms, the closed form and GRPO, all rows or the misread rows, with the retention term. Eight runs in 3 min 19 s.
programs.what: Moves a trained head to a new corpus without losing what it knows. exact_loss fits the head to softmax(log pi_ref + onehot(y) / beta) at beta 0.3; grpo_advantage and grpo_loss sample four classes per row, centre and scale the rewards within the group and take the policy gradient with beta 0.1 on the KL to the starting head. Under both a retention term, the forward KL on the head's own development rows, holds the old readings. Half of the new corpus is held out by group; --rows wrong trains only on the misread rows of the training half. CH-05 of the chain: the eight runs; the two shipped GRPO stages repeated on three seeds.

arch.d: home rows and the new corpus
half by group, or the misread rows
forward KL on home development rows

meetings.note: The closed form and GRPO side by side at the Sprint 3 review.
84.4 (sd 0.2) for 78.8 kept; the dialogue head at 78.6 with its emotion reading intact.

programs.summary: The linear control: ridge logistic regression on the same 2,048 features, the network's folds and confirmation rows, paired by the corrected t-test.
programs.what: Reads the network's folds.csv and confirmation ids so that the control sees exactly the same rows, chooses C on two folds, fits the multinomial logit with L-BFGS on every fold and seed, scores the confirmation split and SEntFiN, and pairs the fold-by-seed macro-F1 against the network with the corrected resampled t-test and a paired bootstrap. CH-06: 66 min 42 s, the longest job of the chain (L-BFGS makes several hundred passes over a 360 MB matrix per fit).

arch.d: the network's folds.csv and confirmation ids

meetings.note: +0.018 macro-F1 for the hidden layers on FinGPT, p 5e-8; a tie on the dialogue data.

programs.summary: The word logit: a multinomial logit on word indicators, identified by its ridge penalty, one model per corpus, with its trigger words. The control for the encoder.
programs.what: words_of reads the distinct words of a text; indicators builds the sparse matrix; fit_logit fits the multinomial logit with L2 by L-BFGS with C chosen by grouped cross-validation; read and predict score a text word by word with N/A for a text with no known word; trigger_words lists the words whose top class probability exceeds 0.5 (4,648 on SEntFiN). CH-07: 7 min 31 s for the three models. The trigger table is written with six decimals after a word at 0.50004 recomputed on the other side of 0.5.

meetings.note: FinGPT at 71.0, SEntFiN at 58.9 zero-shot and 79.8 in domain.
A word at 0.50004 recomputed on the other side of 0.5; six decimals now.

programs.file: slurm/_header.sh, encode.sh, train.sh, predict.sh, adapt.sh, linear.sh, words.sh
programs.summary: The job scripts with their allocations; the shared header writes one dated PASS or FAIL line with the wall time to the chain log.
programs.what: Each job script sets its stage id and reference, sources env/paths.sh and _header.sh, and runs its script. _header.sh records the node, the allocation and the Python in the job's own log, traps the exit and appends one dated line with the duration to logs/chain_<date>.log. The configuration travels as a positional argument, because sbatch does not pass environment variables into a job: the second fault of 3 November, when both training jobs trained the finance head.

meetings.note: Two CH-03 lines in the chain log: sbatch does not pass environment variables into a job.

programs.summary: The whole chain as one submission: prepare on the login node, then seven jobs with afterok dependencies, the integration test last.
programs.what: Runs prepare for both configs, then submits encode, the two training jobs, adapt, linear and words with afterok dependencies, and the integration test depending on all of them, so the test never runs on a partial tree. Submitted four times on 2 and 3 November: the environment fault, the positional config, three checker fixes against the real tree, the mutation count; the fourth submission ended with CH-08 PASS, 154 checks, and the archive was packed and its checksum verified.

meetings.note: Submissions one and two failed on the environment and the configuration.
Submission four: 154 PASS, 8 FAIL on the broken copy, exit 0 on the clean tree.

programs.summary: Every function of common/* against closed-form answers, and the torch head against an independent numpy pass: the parity oracle.
programs.what: UT-D covers the cleaning branches, UT-B the word reader, UT-N the grouping, the confirmation split and the corrected t-test on known values, UT-E the window count at 1, 509, 510, 511, 988 and 989 tokens with a tiny random encoder from make_tiny.py, UT-R the closed-form tilt and the GRPO advantage, UT-G the dated log. numpy_head.py reruns an exported head without torch and is the oracle the integration test and the application's parity tests rest on. conftest.py writes logs/unit_<date>.log, .json and a junit xml. 111 passed in 15.4 seconds on 3 November.

programs.summary: The whole chain on synthetic data with a tiny random encoder, 25 steps in under three minutes, run on the login node before anything is submitted.
programs.what: Builds synthetic corpora and the tiny encoder, runs prepare, encode, train and predict for both configs, the eight adaptations, the two linear controls, the three word logits, then the integration checker on the result tree (154 checks, no bounds) and on a copy broken five ways (8 FAIL lines, exit 1). run_local.sh runs the unit suite then the smoke chain. It is the layer that exposed the mutation-count fault before the fourth submission.

programs.summary: 154 checks over every model's files: schema, parity to 1e-6, split hygiene, the bounds of the design document. The last job of the chain.
programs.what: Opens each of the fourteen model directories (ten checks each) and runs fourteen checks across models: the export reloads, the numpy pass equals the torch pass and the stored number to 1e-6, confirmation ids are disjoint from every training fold and shared with the controls, the learning log has steps = epochs x ceil(rows / batch), the GRPO trunk differs from its start while mean, sd and temperatures do not, the confirmation score lies inside the cross-validation band, and every headline number of the document holds to its bound in bounds.json. Writes results/integration_report.txt and exits 0 or 1; integration_test.sh runs it as CH-08.

steps, moved trunk, fixed mean and sd

programs.summary: Five faults seeded into a copy of the results; the checker must fail with exactly 8 FAIL lines and exit 1.
programs.what: M1 appends a confirmation id to a training fold, M2 lowers a stored accuracy by 0.01, M3 replaces a GRPO trunk by its start, M4 truncates a bias vector, M5 removes the trigger word copra. Each fault maps to a different check, so the run shows the checker's coverage. The first version raised the accuracy, which also crossed the upper bound and gave 9 FAIL lines, and a doubled submission made the day's log count 16; both fixed on 3 November.

programs.summary: Nothing leaves the SuperComputer carrying a login, a host name or a project path: the forbidden-pattern tests and the static scan of every deliverable.
programs.what: A test over every export, summary and log that refuses a file carrying a home path, a login or an address (NF-07 and ST-F-07 on the application side), and a static scan run over every document, slide and figure before it leaves. The public repository carries the login redacted; the result files carry paths relative to the project root only.

programs.summary: The Streamlit application: a sentence through any of the fourteen models, the network drawn with its live activations, the word logit word by word.
programs.what: Hara's application, built from the first experiments of 12 October to the first deployment of 25 October and the redeployment of all fourteen models on 1 November. It reads the model store, calls the encoder service for a new sentence, runs the heads on a CPU with the same numpy pass the unit tests use, draws the network a sentence passes through with the calculation steps, and reads a sentence word by word for the word logit with N/A for unknown words. 368 statements, 99 percent covered.

meetings.note: First Streamlit experiments shown at the Sprint 1 review.
The FinGPT Network export read into the page.
The Dialogue Network page and the adapted heads.
